Enumerate roots in their retained source occurrence order; within a structured value visit arrays in index order and object keys in unsigned Unicode-scalar order. A canonical mirror of the same originating field is visited only once, using the originating field; separately supplied equal values are separate occurrences.

For every supplied artifact occurrence, emit one inventory unit. Where exact bytes are valid UTF-8 and the text projection re-encodes to those exact bytes, also emit physical content units: scan left to right, treating CRLF as one terminator and otherwise CR, LF or form feed as a terminator; each unit contains the span through its terminator. Retain every nonempty span, including blank lines; emit a final unterminated span if present, but no zero-length trailing span. Coordinates start at page 1/line 1; form feed increments page and resets line to 1, other terminators increment line. BOM bytes, if present, remain part of the exact projection, not silently removed. This rule is accounting, not a claim that every UTF-8 artifact's media semantics have been parsed.

For a mechanically supported structured-media subdivision, emit one structural unit per exposed page, section, archive member, embedded document/object, comment, annotation, tracked change or metadata object, using its exact parent and source locator; traverse children in source order, breaking any absent source-order tie by unsigned Unicode-scalar locator order. Recurse into textual leaves using the physical-content rule and into child media using this rule. A structural node is counted once per occurrence/location/kind; a node's structural unit and its descendant content units are distinct. Preserve inaccessible exposed nodes as INACCESSIBLE_OR_BLOCKED; do not fabricate children. Detailed coverage requires a closed format mapping that is part of this named versioned normative algorithm or an explicitly identified versioned normative format mapping authorized under §34.3. Merely publishing an implementation descriptor does not authorize such semantics. The mapping must fix node kinds, source locators, ordering, exact canonical source values and child extraction. This insertion adds no format-specific adapter or mapping. A claim of supported detailed coverage without that normative mapping is blocked; genuinely unsupported formats retain the fallback below. A mechanically available subdivision cannot be suppressed or relabeled unsupported to avoid that blocker.

Subdivision is additive: an exact UTF-8 whole-file projection emits its physical spans even when a supported structured mapping also emits structural nodes and textual leaves. Whole-file spans, structural nodes and structural textual-leaf spans have distinct kinds and locators and are all counted; overlap in underlying bytes does not deduplicate these different accounting obligations. Each archive-member or embedded-file occurrence emits both its parent structural occurrence unit and its own child inventory unit, followed by its own supported content/subdivisions. A textual leaf is not a child file and gets no inventory unit. Repeated references to the same emitted unit still deduplicate under the rule below.

Source hashes and binding are closed as follows. C(x) means the exact UTF-8 bytes of §34.1 canonical JSON; H(b) means lowercase SHA-256 hexadecimal of exact bytes b. Source-value hash preimages by kind are:

- ARTIFACT_INVENTORY: C({"byteLength":n,"contentSha256":h}), where n is exact byte length and h=H(exact artifact bytes). If bytes are unavailable, both values are null; asserted length/digest remains source context, never substituted for observed bytes. The unit remains inaccessible/blocked, with its retained occurrence/locator binding.

- PHYSICAL_SPAN: the exact original byte span including its terminator, without canonical JSON wrapping. Its locator binds zero-based byte start and exclusive end plus the one-based page/line coordinates.

- STRUCTURAL_NODE: C({"nodeKind":k,"status":q,"value":v}), where k and v are the exact kind and canonical source value fixed by the authorized format mapping, and q is ACCESSIBLE or INACCESSIBLE_OR_BLOCKED. Inaccessible nodes have v=null; exact exposed parent/locator and k remain bound. No invented serialization of an adapter object is permitted.

- STRUCTURAL_TEXT_SPAN: exact UTF-8 bytes of the mapped exact textual leaf's physical span, including its terminator. The authorized mapping identifies the leaf and its exact extraction; no silent whitespace normalization is allowed.

Each unit's binding hash preimage is C({"algorithm":"closed-loop-raw-units/1","inputVersion":V,"occurrence":O,"kind":K,"locator":L,"sourceValueSha256":S}). V is the exact owning input-version identity string; O is the ordered zero-based safe-integer path of supplied root and, where applicable, child-member occurrence indices; K is exactly one of the seven uppercase kinds above; S is the corresponding source-value hash. L is an ordered locator array: human units use [originating JSON pointer, one-based physical line] or [originating JSON pointer] for whole strings/scalars; inventories use []; whole-file spans use [startByte,endByte,page,line]; structural nodes use [normative format mapping ID, exact mapping locator]; structural textual spans append [startByte,endByte,page,line] to their structural-leaf locator. Byte offsets for a structural textual leaf refer to its exact UTF-8 extraction. The source-value hash alone does not identify the occurrence: binding hash plus retained input/source supplies the exact type, location and occurrence. These accounting hashes/locators are not §34.2 canonical record IDs. Distinct roots are numbered in retained source occurrence order, including separately supplied identical roots; a canonical mirror does not receive a second root number.

An image/media occurrence without a supported finer subdivision uses its inventory unit as its whole-media unit. A format with no supported mechanically available subdivision likewise uses its inventory unit as the whole-file fallback, with an explicit unsupported/unavailable-subdivision basis and the original bytes retained. These fallbacks neither prove inspection nor remove existing material uncertainty/blockers. Comments, annotations, tracked changes, metadata and embedded content are not discarded as nonsemantic.

Deduplicate only repeated accounting references to the same occurrence, kind, location and exact source-value hash. Never merge distinct supplied occurrences, even with identical hashes. Order and retained source identity determine stable accounting references; canonical record IDs still use §34.2. Count the entire resulting unit universe, including inventory, structural and inaccessible units, when applying the unchanged §6.5A limits. The raw-unit challenge condition is strictly greater than 500, not greater than or equal to 500; every other size-independent trigger remains effective.

Intermediate step outputs exist only for the current execution unless explicitly emitted as observations or evidence.

primarySourceLocation.controllingText: SORT accepts a homogeneous array and optional domain STRING, BOOLEAN, INTEGER or DECIMAL and optional direction ASC or DESC. Omitted domain is inferred from the first element (empty array: STRING); omitted direction is ASC. Strings compare by unsigned Unicode-scalar sequence, Boolean false precedes true, integers compare exactly, and DECIMAL values compare the exact plain-decimal value of {"numberType":"DECIMAL","value":"..."}. obligations.statement: PARSE_JSON accepts standard JSON syntax with unique decoded object member names and scalar-valid strings.

primarySourceLocation.controllingText: PARSE_JSON accepts standard JSON syntax with unique decoded object member names and scalar-valid strings. Numeric tokens are restricted to -?(0|[1-9][0-9]*) in the inclusive range -9007199254740991 through 9007199254740991, excluding -0; decimal points/exponents are unsupported even if the mathematical value is integral. Test IR is a topologically ordered directed acyclic graph. Every step has a unique application-validated stepId, one registered op, and an explicit inputs object. Each input references exactly one literal, immutable binding, or prior step output. A step may reference only an earlier step. Hidden accumulators, implicit stacks, ambient project state, ambient current values, operand-by-position rules, and implementation-dependent input selection are prohibited.

Every registered operation declares named input ports, output ports, exact types, cardinalities, deterministic error codes, error propagation, and resource-cost category. Each operation declares exact input arity and types and one normalized output type. Multi-artifact branches use explicit step references. BYTE_COMPARE and COMPARE receive explicit left and right inputs. Assertions receive explicit actual and expected inputs. A failed or unknown predecessor prevents dependent execution and propagates the registered terminal disposition without partial canonical result; errors propagate as typed execution failure and no later step may consume a failed output. Intermediate step outputs exist only for the current execution unless explicitly emitted as observations or evidence.

DECIMAL_STRING equality requires two plain decimal strings matching [+-]?[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)? after removal of surrounding ASCII U+0009–U+000D/U+0020 whitespace; compare mathematically exactly, ignoring leading plus/zeros and trailing fractional zeros. Ordered COMPARE operators and ASSERT_GT/GTE/LT/LTE use exact ordering of two safe integers or two such decimal strings. COMPARE with ordered operators accepts omitted mode or INTEGER for that ordinary exact domain; explicit DECIMAL_STRING restricts both operands to those strings. Ordered comparisons reject APPROXIMATE and every tolerance argument at definition admission. All EQ/NE/ASSERT_EQ comparisons outside APPROXIMATE also reject tolerance arguments, including compatibility aliases. No binary-float approximation or exponent is implicit.

primarySourceLocation.controllingText: APPROXIMATE applies only to COMPARE EQ/NE or ASSERT_EQ and requires an explicit absTol or relTol (or its compatibility alias). Operands and tolerances accept a JSON safe integer other than negative zero, a canonical plain decimal string as just defined, or that exact typed DECIMAL object. Operands may be negative; tolerances must be mathematically nonnegative. At least one tolerance component is explicit; the omitted component is zero. Use exact arithmetic: |actual-expected| <= max(absTol, relTol × max(|actual|,|expected|)). Approximate NE is the logical complement of that equality result. Compatibility names absoluteTolerance and relativeTolerance map to absTol and relTol; when both names for a component appear they must normalize to exactly the same mathematical value, otherwise reject the definition. Unsupported precision is UNDETERMINED. These aliases authorize no other default.

Test IR is a topologically ordered directed acyclic graph. Every step has a unique application-validated stepId, one registered op, and an explicit inputs object. Each input references exactly one literal, immutable binding, or prior step output. A step may reference only an earlier step. Hidden accumulators, implicit stacks, ambient project state, ambient current values, operand-by-position rules, and implementation-dependent input selection are prohibited.

Every registered operation declares named input ports, output ports, exact types, cardinalities, deterministic error codes, error propagation, and resource-cost category. Each operation declares exact input arity and types and one normalized output type. Multi-artifact branches use explicit step references. BYTE_COMPARE and COMPARE receive explicit left and right inputs. Assertions receive explicit actual and expected inputs. A failed or unknown predecessor prevents dependent execution and propagates the registered terminal disposition without partial canonical result; errors propagate as typed execution failure and no later step may consume a failed output. Intermediate step outputs exist only for the current execution unless explicitly emitted as observations or evidence.

obligations.statement: XML selectors start with exactly one slash, then child-element segments named [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.:-]* or *, optionally followed by [positive safe integer].

primarySourceLocation.controllingText: XML selectors start with exactly one slash, then child-element segments named [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.:-]* or *, optionally followed by [positive safe integer]. The first segment matches the document element at position 1; later positions apply within each parent's matching child elements. Only the final segment may be @name or text(). Element results are arrays of the canonical element-node values defined in D4; attribute results are arrays of existing exact attribute strings; text() returns one string per selected element, concatenating descendant text/CDATA in document order and excluding comments. A wholly empty selection at any segment, including a final attribute selection, is UNDETERMINED. A selected element with no text yields the known empty string, not a missing selection. Other selector syntax is invalid before execution.

primarySourceLocation.controllingText: PARSE_CSV requires explicit delimiter, quote, header, newline and encoding. Delimiter and quote are distinct single Unicode scalars other than CR/LF; header is Boolean; encoding is UTF-8; newline is AUTO, LF, CRLF or CR. AUTO accepts CRLF as one newline and otherwise CR or LF. A quoted cell starts at the beginning of its field, doubles quote characters for one literal quote, preserves quoted newlines, and allows only delimiter, contracted newline or end after closing quote. Other unquoted CR/LF is malformed. Empty input yields []; a final newline does not create an extra row; blank rows contain one empty cell; a trailing delimiter creates an empty final cell. Header false yields row arrays; header true consumes the first row as unique exact header names and requires equal subsequent widths. No cell type inference occurs.

obligations.statement: PARSE_XML returns the document element as a canonical JSON object with exactly four required non-null properties: name (exact element-name string), attributes (object of exact parsed attribute-name/string-value pairs), children (ordered array of its immediate element-node values), and content (ordered array of strings and immediate element-node values in source content order).

primarySourceLocation.controllingText: PARSE_XML returns the document element as a canonical JSON object with exactly four required non-null properties: name (exact element-name string), attributes (object of exact parsed attribute-name/string-value pairs), children (ordered array of its immediate element-node values), and content (ordered array of strings and immediate element-node values in source content order). Every child appears once in children and once as the same canonical value in content; this is duplicated value content, not a cyclic pointer or identity-based equality. Each nonempty ordinary text run between markup boundaries contributes one decoded string; each nonempty CDATA body contributes one literal string. Empty runs are omitted, comments contribute no entry, adjacent strings separated by comment/CDATA boundaries are not coalesced, and entity references within a text run are decoded into that one string. Outside-root whitespace and the declaration are not represented. Attribute order has no canonical-equality significance; child/content array order and text-run segmentation do. Thus differently ordered attributes with equal values compare equal, while mixed text/child content remains observable in exact document order. XML name/attribute/character normalization is precisely the parsing rule above, not namespace inference.

Every child appears once in children and once as the same canonical value in content; this is duplicated value content, not a cyclic pointer or identity-based equality. Each nonempty ordinary text run between markup boundaries contributes one decoded string; each nonempty CDATA body contributes one literal string. Empty runs are omitted, comments contribute no entry, adjacent strings separated by comment/CDATA boundaries are not coalesced, and entity references within a text run are decoded into that one string. Outside-root whitespace and the declaration are not represented. Attribute order has no canonical-equality significance; child/content array order and text-run segmentation do. Thus differently ordered attributes with equal values compare equal, while mixed text/child content remains observable in exact document order. XML name/attribute/character normalization is precisely the parsing rule above, not namespace inference.

ASSERT_MATCH asserts the same Boolean regex result as REGEX using actual/pattern/optional flags; ordered assertions use the exact ordering above. Each assertion yields only SATISFIED or VIOLATED on valid data, with other terminal dispositions propagated as D5 states. The optional message on assertions is a non-null string, absent by default, used only as diagnostic text and never to alter a result. SORT/UNIQUE require arrays and return arrays; MIN/MAX/SUM require arrays as stated. HASH_SHA256 requires bytes; REGEX requires string value/pattern; selectors require a string path and the defined structured value. Unknown optional arguments and implicit operand/binding selection are prohibited. Authoring shortcuts remain permitted only when they compile to the identical explicit §21.3 DAG and named ports. Each input references exactly one literal, immutable binding, or prior step output. A step may reference only an earlier step. Hidden accumulators, implicit stacks, ambient project state, ambient current values, operand-by-position rules, and implementation-dependent input selection are prohibited.

Every registered operation declares named input ports, output ports, exact types, cardinalities, deterministic error codes, error propagation, and resource-cost category. Each operation declares exact input arity and types and one normalized output type. Multi-artifact branches use explicit step references. BYTE_COMPARE and COMPARE receive explicit left and right inputs. Assertions receive explicit actual and expected inputs. A failed or unknown predecessor prevents dependent execution and propagates the registered terminal disposition without partial canonical result; errors propagate as typed execution failure and no later step may consume a failed output. Intermediate step outputs exist only for the current execution unless explicitly emitted as observations or evidence.

The author and reviewer cannot share the same raw response, context reservation, operation reservation, or accepted review identity. A reviewer cannot approve a semantic value it authored. Search adequacy, Stage 03 extraction challenge, Stage 04 disposition and atomicity, Stage 05 classification/applicability/equivalence, Stage 06 proof-expression, evidence-basis, and native-versus-external representability review, and Stage 26 semantic reconciliation use this contract.

When author and reviewer disagree materially, neither output is promoted. A distinct reconciliation operation is required, and a distinct reconciler receives both completed outputs and the governing evidence. The reconciler differs from both contexts unless a genuine human-authority decision is required. A third reviewer is required when the reconciliation contract designates the dispute as technical semantic judgment and neither prior view can be rejected from objective evidence. A human may decide only an actual human authority, policy, scope, risk, disclosure, or tradeoff question. Every unresolved disagreement remains UNKNOWN or BLOCKED and is never automatically promoted.

Materiality is MATERIAL, NONMATERIAL, or UNKNOWN. MATERIAL means the item could change the truth value, applicability, proof admissibility, evidence sufficiency, identity, due state, dependency closure, gate result, authorization, or delivery status of at least one current release-bearing proposition or action. NONMATERIAL requires affirmative reasoning that the item cannot alter any current proposition, proof obligation, artifact identity, dependency, gate, release eligibility, delivery scope, or delivery state. UNKNOWN is treated as MATERIAL for exclusion and blocking. Every materiality determination that excludes content, reduces required work, or downgrades an obligation is recorded as a materialityReviews record; where it reduces a possible obligation it requires independent review under Section 26.5.

Every normalizer and application derivation has an immutable registry ID, version, implementation-owner file, canonical input contract, output contract, hash or build identity, and invalidation consequences. Every derived value records the exact derivation ID and source-record hashes. A changed normalizer or derivation invalidates affected current values and results unless an explicit compatibility migration proves byte- and semantic-equivalent output.

Every release-bearing derivation and normalizer is completely defined by this specification or by an explicitly named versioned normative algorithm. The semantics defined in Sections 14.6, 15, 16.1, 26, 29, 30, 31, 34.1, 34.2, and 36 control their registry entries, and an entry cannot deviate from them. A release-bearing derivation or normalizer whose semantics are not so defined is UNDEFINED_DERIVATION and blocks acceptance.

Unknown extension data preserves the exact original bytes whenever those bytes exist. If only a parsed representation is available, the application preserves the closed canonical representation together with original source digest, parser identity and version, source location, and the explicit reason original bytes were unavailable. The implementation MUST NOT choose arbitrarily between byte-for-byte and canonical preservation; exact original bytes control whenever they exist. Unknown extension data remains non-operational, non-gating, non-executable, excluded from prompts by default, and incapable of acquiring trust without an explicit schema migration.

Completion: Every due PER_RUN_REQUIRED mandatory proposition has one comparison covering all ten current runs under its frozen expected-variance contract. Allowed variance is recorded; prohibited variance has a defect; UNKNOWN variance remains blocked.
- AGENT owns proposed semantic dimensions and rationale; APPLICATION owns identity, normalized contract, frozen timing, scope, hash, and evaluation use.

humanInputRequests is a required, non-null ordered array, empty allowed. No item property is nullable. All strings preserve their supplied scalar values; nonblank means containing at least one character outside U+0009–U+000D and U+0020.

The author and reviewer cannot share the same raw response, context reservation, operation reservation, or accepted review identity. A reviewer cannot approve a semantic value it authored. Search adequacy, Stage 03 extraction challenge, Stage 04 disposition and atomicity, Stage 05 classification/applicability/equivalence, Stage 06 proof-expression, evidence-basis, and native-versus-external representability review, and Stage 26 semantic reconciliation use this contract.

When author and reviewer disagree materially, neither output is promoted. A distinct reconciliation operation is required, and a distinct reconciler receives both completed outputs and the governing evidence. The reconciler differs from both contexts unless a genuine human-authority decision is required. A third reviewer is required when the reconciliation contract designates the dispute as technical semantic judgment and neither prior view can be rejected from objective evidence. A human may decide only an actual human authority, policy, scope, risk, disclosure, or tradeoff question. Every unresolved disagreement remains UNKNOWN or BLOCKED and is never automatically promoted.

Materiality is MATERIAL, NONMATERIAL, or UNKNOWN. MATERIAL means the item could change the truth value, applicability, proof admissibility, evidence sufficiency, identity, due state, dependency closure, gate result, authorization, or delivery status of at least one current release-bearing proposition or action. NONMATERIAL requires affirmative reasoning that the item cannot alter any current proposition, proof obligation, artifact identity, dependency, gate, release eligibility, delivery scope, or delivery state. UNKNOWN is treated as MATERIAL for exclusion and blocking. Every materiality determination that excludes content, reduces required work, or downgrades an obligation is recorded as a materialityReviews record; where it reduces a possible obligation it requires independent review under Section 26.5.

Every normalizer and application derivation has an immutable registry ID, version, implementation-owner file, canonical input contract, output contract, hash or build identity, and invalidation consequences. Every derived value records the exact derivation ID and source-record hashes. A changed normalizer or derivation invalidates affected current values and results unless an explicit compatibility migration proves byte- and semantic-equivalent output.

Every release-bearing derivation and normalizer is completely defined by this specification or by an explicitly named versioned normative algorithm. The semantics defined in Sections 14.6, 15, 16.1, 26, 29, 30, 31, 34.1, 34.2, and 36 control their registry entries, and an entry cannot deviate from them. A release-bearing derivation or normalizer whose semantics are not so defined is UNDEFINED_DERIVATION and blocks acceptance.

Unknown extension data preserves the exact original bytes whenever those bytes exist. If only a parsed representation is available, the application preserves the closed canonical representation together with original source digest, parser identity and version, source location, and the explicit reason original bytes were unavailable. The implementation MUST NOT choose arbitrarily between byte-for-byte and canonical preservation; exact original bytes control whenever they exist. Unknown extension data remains non-operational, non-gating, non-executable, excluded from prompts by default, and incapable of acquiring trust without an explicit schema migration.

Completion: Every due PER_RUN_REQUIRED mandatory proposition has one comparison covering all ten current runs under its frozen expected-variance contract. Allowed variance is recorded; prohibited variance has a defect; UNKNOWN variance remains blocked.
- AGENT owns proposed semantic dimensions and rationale; APPLICATION owns identity, normalized contract, frozen timing, scope, hash, and evaluation use.

humanInputRequests is a required, non-null ordered array, empty allowed. Each item is a closed object with exactly these required properties: temporaryKey, question, whyRequired, affectedStageFields, affectedRecords, answerType, allowedValues; its only optional property is blocking. No item property is nullable. All strings preserve their supplied scalar values; nonblank means containing at least one character outside U+0009–U+000D and U+0020.

obligations.statement: Accepted authoring forms are (1) records.tests[i].fields.EXPECTED_VARIANCE_CONTRACT, an embedded object with those lower-camel-case names, and (2) records.expectedVarianceContracts[i].fields.DIMENSIONS, .ALLOWED_VARIANCE and optional .RATIONALE, with TEST_ID in that record's relationships member.

primarySourceLocation.controllingText: Accepted authoring forms are (1) records.tests[i].fields.EXPECTED_VARIANCE_CONTRACT, an embedded object with those lower-camel-case names, and (2) records.expectedVarianceContracts[i].fields.DIMENSIONS, .ALLOWED_VARIANCE and optional .RATIONALE, with TEST_ID in that record's relationships member. The latter is exactly relationships.TEST_ID = {"tempKey":"<same-response tests tempKey>"} or {"recordId":"<operation-supplied current tests ID>"}, resolved through the existing ingestion path. No direct authored application-owned TEST_ID field is accepted. Map only those three direct names to their lower-camel-case counterparts. Embedded additional canonical-JSON properties are preserved exactly and included in the semantic hash as nonoperative context; they cannot introduce executable meaning, a gate, evidence basis or favorable outcome. Direct records remain subject to their closed family registry; no arbitrary new direct field is permitted. If both forms address a test, their normalized objects must be canonical-byte-identical; disagreement or ambiguous duplicates block rather than choosing a winner. Byte-identical embedded and direct forms for the same resolved test produce exactly one current enclosing contract retaining provenance from both sources, never competing canonical contracts. Section 35.10 continues to require preservation of original extension bytes where available and default prompt exclusion. Hashing retained context establishes identity and invalidation only, never permission to execute it or to count it as favorable evidence.

Accepted authoring forms are (1) records.tests[i].fields.EXPECTED_VARIANCE_CONTRACT, an embedded object with those lower-camel-case names, and (2) records.expectedVarianceContracts[i].fields.DIMENSIONS, .ALLOWED_VARIANCE and optional .RATIONALE, with TEST_ID in that record's relationships member. The latter is exactly relationships.TEST_ID = {"tempKey":"<same-response tests tempKey>"} or {"recordId":"<operation-supplied current tests ID>"}, resolved through the existing ingestion path. No direct authored application-owned TEST_ID field is accepted. Map only those three direct names to their lower-camel-case counterparts. Embedded additional canonical-JSON properties are preserved exactly and included in the semantic hash as nonoperative context; they cannot introduce executable meaning, a gate, evidence basis or favorable outcome. Direct records remain subject to their closed family registry; no arbitrary new direct field is permitted. If both forms address a test, their normalized objects must be canonical-byte-identical; disagreement or ambiguous duplicates block rather than choosing a winner. Byte-identical embedded and direct forms for the same resolved test produce exactly one current enclosing contract retaining provenance from both sources, never competing canonical contracts. Section 35.10 continues to require preservation of original extension bytes where available and default prompt exclusion. Hashing retained context establishes identity and invalidation only, never permission to execute it or to count it as favorable evidence.

The author and reviewer cannot share the same raw response, context reservation, operation reservation, or accepted review identity. A reviewer cannot approve a semantic value it authored. Search adequacy, Stage 03 extraction challenge, Stage 04 disposition and atomicity, Stage 05 classification/applicability/equivalence, Stage 06 proof-expression, evidence-basis, and native-versus-external representability review, and Stage 26 semantic reconciliation use this contract.

When author and reviewer disagree materially, neither output is promoted. A distinct reconciliation operation is required, and a distinct reconciler receives both completed outputs and the governing evidence. The reconciler differs from both contexts unless a genuine human-authority decision is required. A third reviewer is required when the reconciliation contract designates the dispute as technical semantic judgment and neither prior view can be rejected from objective evidence. A human may decide only an actual human authority, policy, scope, risk, disclosure, or tradeoff question. Every unresolved disagreement remains UNKNOWN or BLOCKED and is never automatically promoted.

Materiality is MATERIAL, NONMATERIAL, or UNKNOWN. MATERIAL means the item could change the truth value, applicability, proof admissibility, evidence sufficiency, identity, due state, dependency closure, gate result, authorization, or delivery status of at least one current release-bearing proposition or action. NONMATERIAL requires affirmative reasoning that the item cannot alter any current proposition, proof obligation, artifact identity, dependency, gate, release eligibility, delivery scope, or delivery state. UNKNOWN is treated as MATERIAL for exclusion and blocking. Every materiality determination that excludes content, reduces required work, or downgrades an obligation is recorded as a materialityReviews record; where it reduces a possible obligation it requires independent review under Section 26.5.

Every normalizer and application derivation has an immutable registry ID, version, implementation-owner file, canonical input contract, output contract, hash or build identity, and invalidation consequences. Every derived value records the exact derivation ID and source-record hashes. A changed normalizer or derivation invalidates affected current values and results unless an explicit compatibility migration proves byte- and semantic-equivalent output.

Every release-bearing derivation and normalizer is completely defined by this specification or by an explicitly named versioned normative algorithm. The semantics defined in Sections 14.6, 15, 16.1, 26, 29, 30, 31, 34.1, 34.2, and 36 control their registry entries, and an entry cannot deviate from them. A release-bearing derivation or normalizer whose semantics are not so defined is UNDEFINED_DERIVATION and blocks acceptance.

Unknown extension data preserves the exact original bytes whenever those bytes exist. If only a parsed representation is available, the application preserves the closed canonical representation together with original source digest, parser identity and version, source location, and the explicit reason original bytes were unavailable. The implementation MUST NOT choose arbitrarily between byte-for-byte and canonical preservation; exact original bytes control whenever they exist. Unknown extension data remains non-operational, non-gating, non-executable, excluded from prompts by default, and incapable of acquiring trust without an explicit schema migration.

Completion: Every due PER_RUN_REQUIRED mandatory proposition has one comparison covering all ten current runs under its frozen expected-variance contract. Allowed variance is recorded; prohibited variance has a defect; UNKNOWN variance remains blocked.

Byte-identical embedded and direct forms for the same resolved test produce exactly one current enclosing contract retaining provenance from both sources, never competing canonical contracts. Section 35.10 continues to require preservation of original extension bytes where available and default prompt exclusion. Hashing retained context establishes identity and invalidation only, never permission to execute it or to count it as favorable evidence.

The author and reviewer cannot share the same raw response, context reservation, operation reservation, or accepted review identity. A reviewer cannot approve a semantic value it authored. Search adequacy, Stage 03 extraction challenge, Stage 04 disposition and atomicity, Stage 05 classification/applicability/equivalence, Stage 06 proof-expression, evidence-basis, and native-versus-external representability review, and Stage 26 semantic reconciliation use this contract.

When author and reviewer disagree materially, neither output is promoted. A distinct reconciliation operation is required, and a distinct reconciler receives both completed outputs and the governing evidence. The reconciler differs from both contexts unless a genuine human-authority decision is required. A third reviewer is required when the reconciliation contract designates the dispute as technical semantic judgment and neither prior view can be rejected from objective evidence. A human may decide only an actual human authority, policy, scope, risk, disclosure, or tradeoff question. Every unresolved disagreement remains UNKNOWN or BLOCKED and is never automatically promoted.

Materiality is MATERIAL, NONMATERIAL, or UNKNOWN. MATERIAL means the item could change the truth value, applicability, proof admissibility, evidence sufficiency, identity, due state, dependency closure, gate result, authorization, or delivery status of at least one current release-bearing proposition or action. NONMATERIAL requires affirmative reasoning that the item cannot alter any current proposition, proof obligation, artifact identity, dependency, gate, release eligibility, delivery scope, or delivery state. UNKNOWN is treated as MATERIAL for exclusion and blocking. Every materiality determination that excludes content, reduces required work, or downgrades an obligation is recorded as a materialityReviews record; where it reduces a possible obligation it requires independent review under Section 26.5.

Every normalizer and application derivation has an immutable registry ID, version, implementation-owner file, canonical input contract, output contract, hash or build identity, and invalidation consequences. Every derived value records the exact derivation ID and source-record hashes. A changed normalizer or derivation invalidates affected current values and results unless an explicit compatibility migration proves byte- and semantic-equivalent output.

Every release-bearing derivation and normalizer is completely defined by this specification or by an explicitly named versioned normative algorithm. The semantics defined in Sections 14.6, 15, 16.1, 26, 29, 30, 31, 34.1, 34.2, and 36 control their registry entries, and an entry cannot deviate from them. A release-bearing derivation or normalizer whose semantics are not so defined is UNDEFINED_DERIVATION and blocks acceptance.

Unknown extension data preserves the exact original bytes whenever those bytes exist. If only a parsed representation is available, the application preserves the closed canonical representation together with original source digest, parser identity and version, source location, and the explicit reason original bytes were unavailable. The implementation MUST NOT choose arbitrarily between byte-for-byte and canonical preservation; exact original bytes control whenever they exist. Unknown extension data remains non-operational, non-gating, non-executable, excluded from prompts by default, and incapable of acquiring trust without an explicit schema migration.

Completion: Every due PER_RUN_REQUIRED mandatory proposition has one comparison covering all ten current runs under its frozen expected-variance contract. Allowed variance is recorded; prohibited variance has a defect; UNKNOWN variance remains blocked.

The author and reviewer cannot share the same raw response, context reservation, operation reservation, or accepted review identity. A reviewer cannot approve a semantic value it authored. Search adequacy, Stage 03 extraction challenge, Stage 04 disposition and atomicity, Stage 05 classification/applicability/equivalence, Stage 06 proof-expression, evidence-basis, and native-versus-external representability review, and Stage 26 semantic reconciliation use this contract.

When author and reviewer disagree materially, neither output is promoted. A distinct reconciliation operation is required, and a distinct reconciler receives both completed outputs and the governing evidence. The reconciler differs from both contexts unless a genuine human-authority decision is required. A third reviewer is required when the reconciliation contract designates the dispute as technical semantic judgment and neither prior view can be rejected from objective evidence. A human may decide only an actual human authority, policy, scope, risk, disclosure, or tradeoff question. Every unresolved disagreement remains UNKNOWN or BLOCKED and is never automatically promoted.

Materiality is MATERIAL, NONMATERIAL, or UNKNOWN. MATERIAL means the item could change the truth value, applicability, proof admissibility, evidence sufficiency, identity, due state, dependency closure, gate result, authorization, or delivery status of at least one current release-bearing proposition or action. NONMATERIAL requires affirmative reasoning that the item cannot alter any current proposition, proof obligation, artifact identity, dependency, gate, release eligibility, delivery scope, or delivery state. UNKNOWN is treated as MATERIAL for exclusion and blocking. Every materiality determination that excludes content, reduces required work, or downgrades an obligation is recorded as a materialityReviews record; where it reduces a possible obligation it requires independent review under Section 26.5.

Every normalizer and application derivation has an immutable registry ID, version, implementation-owner file, canonical input contract, output contract, hash or build identity, and invalidation consequences. Every derived value records the exact derivation ID and source-record hashes. A changed normalizer or derivation invalidates affected current values and results unless an explicit compatibility migration proves byte- and semantic-equivalent output.

Every release-bearing derivation and normalizer is completely defined by this specification or by an explicitly named versioned normative algorithm. The semantics defined in Sections 14.6, 15, 16.1, 26, 29, 30, 31, 34.1, 34.2, and 36 control their registry entries, and an entry cannot deviate from them. A release-bearing derivation or normalizer whose semantics are not so defined is UNDEFINED_DERIVATION and blocks acceptance.

Unknown extension data preserves the exact original bytes whenever those bytes exist. If only a parsed representation is available, the application preserves the closed canonical representation together with original source digest, parser identity and version, source location, and the explicit reason original bytes were unavailable. The implementation MUST NOT choose arbitrarily between byte-for-byte and canonical preservation; exact original bytes control whenever they exist. Unknown extension data remains non-operational, non-gating, non-executable, excluded from prompts by default, and incapable of acquiring trust without an explicit schema migration.

These are the existing later-than-owning-stage deferred failure-test and regression execution routes. A pair is available only for a current accepted definition and its current accepted, independently reviewed execution-test binding, with established definition/test/fixture/target/outcome compatibility, the declared earliest executable stage reached, and the required current target-availability and phase conditions TRUE. Unknown, stale or unavailable prerequisites block; a legitimately future definition remains visible and unexecuted. Timing, compatibility and authority cannot be supplied by this list or inferred from a route label.

- External-agent operations are COMPLETE at Stages 01-09, 15, 21, 23, 24, 25, and 26; SEMANTIC_CHALLENGE; RECONCILE_INTAKE; SEARCH_ADEQUACY_REVIEW; RECONCILE_SOURCE_SEARCH; RECONCILE_RESEARCH; DISPOSITION_CHALLENGE; ATOMICITY_CHALLENGE; RECONCILE_REQUIREMENTS; SEMANTIC_REVIEW; RECONCILE_REQUIREMENT_SET; PROOF_REVIEW; RECONCILE_VERIFICATION_SUITE; EXECUTE_RUN; VERIFY; COMPARE; ROOT_CAUSE; REGRESSION; CORRECT; RECONCILE at Stage 26; ADVISORY_REVIEW at Stage 27; EXECUTE_EXTERNAL_TEST; INVESTIGATE_MISSING_EVIDENCE; and EXECUTE_FAILURE_TEST, EXECUTE_REGRESSION, and REGRESSION_VERIFY when externally routed. They require an operation reservation and file-first package. Their responseType is exactly DATA_PROPOSAL, HUMAN_INPUT_REQUIRED, BLOCKED, or EXECUTION_FAILED as permitted by the operation's field contract. ADVISORY_REVIEW at Stage 27 is optional and non-gating: it writes releaseGateReviews records only and cannot modify, delay, or substitute for any CALCULATE_RELEASE input, calculation, or state.
- Application commands are EXECUTE_FAILURE_TEST when natively routed, EXECUTE_REGRESSION when natively routed, REGRESSION_VERIFY when natively routed, FREEZE, CONFIRM_FREEZE, COMPLETE at Stage 18, CONFIRM at Stage 19, FREEZE_BASELINE, RUN_NATIVE_TESTS, RUN_NATIVE_ATTACKS, FREEZE_DELIVERY_CANDIDATE, VERIFY_IDENTITY, CALCULATE_RELEASE, CALCULATE_EVIDENCE_CHAINS, and CALCULATE_TERMINAL. They accept no external response envelope and commit only application-owned results through the universal command path. COMPLETE at Stage 18 and CONFIRM at Stage 19 are application-calculated convergence and confirmation determinations; agents contribute only the separately declared explanatory fields of the owning record families. FREEZE, CONFIRM_FREEZE, FREEZE_BASELINE, and FREEZE_DELIVERY_CANDIDATE consume and reference the required current humanDecisions records; they never create human authority.
- HUMAN_DECISION commands are CAPTURE_DELIVERY_INTENT; application confirmation of a newly reported human-origin answer; and RECORD_HUMAN_DECISION, one global application-validated command bound to exactly one registered purpose and target per invocation. The closed RECORD_HUMAN_DECISION purpose enum is INTENT_CONFIRMATION, CANDIDATE_COMPONENT_SELECTION, BASELINE_AUTHORIZATION, DISCLOSURE_AUTHORIZATION, EXTERNAL_ACTION_RISK_AUTHORIZATION, CONTROLLED_EXCEPTION, REGRESSION_RETIREMENT_AUTHORIZATION, BACKUP_POLICY_SELECTION, TRADEOFF_OR_SCOPE_DECISION, VISUAL_BASELINE_AUTHORIZATION, and HUMAN_AUTHORITY_CORRECTION. Each purpose writes only the humanDecisions record and the human-decision-owned fields FIELD_REGISTRY declares for that purpose and target. HUMAN commands are SAVE_HUMAN_INPUT, which creates and edits User Job Input and saves Section 18 fallback answers with their declared consequences, and RECORD_HUMAN_OBSERVATION, which records human-owned observation and evidence records for human-inspection routes. These commands write only their declared HUMAN or HUMAN_DECISION fields and records, accept no agent-owned canonical fields, and accept no external response envelope.
- EXPORT_PROMPT_FILE, EXPORT_EXECUTION_PACKAGE, SELECT_RESPONSE_JSON_FILE, SELECT_RETURNED_FILES, EXPORT_OR_SHARE_AUTHORIZED_ARTIFACTS, and RECORD_DELIVERY_EVIDENCE are operator actions. They create only the application receipts and human or external evidence explicitly declared by their contracts.

For every operation, TARGET_SLOT = SHA-256(closed-loop-canonical-json/1 of contractProfileId, jobId, stage, operation, and all operation-specific target identities required by Section 14.7). The target slot excludes projectRevision so an exact retry retains its slot; expectedRevision and scopeHash remain separate mandatory preconditions. No operation can write a family or field not listed in its FIELD_REGISTRY entry.

A failure or regression test is executed only when its target exists and its current EARLIEST_EXECUTABLE_STAGE has been reached. Its REQUIRED_BY_STAGE may not precede target availability. A not-yet-due test remains registered and visible as future work but does not falsely block a prior convergence stage.

Every negative, mutation, adversarial, storage-failure, parser-hostility, and deliberately invalid fixture executes against isolated disposable state: a test-only project clone, test-only IndexedDB namespace, immutable read-only artifact copy, isolated worker input, or explicitly authorized external sandbox. The suite must prove that no fixture mutated a canonical user project or an unauthorized third-party target. Canonical user projects and third-party systems are never mutation targets unless the exact action is separately authorized and safely bounded.

32.5 Regression retirement

A regression is ACTIVE, SUPERSEDED, or RETIRED. Retirement requires sufficient current evidence that the linked proposition left scope, was replaced so the old mechanism is inapplicable, or the failure mechanism is impossible under the current evidenced architecture; current NOT_APPLICABLE status; required human authorization; independent review; an append-only retirement record; and no current baseline or product dependency. A failing, inconvenient, expensive, unavailable, or flaky regression cannot be retired for that reason. UNKNOWN legitimacy blocks. History is never deleted.

32.5 Regression retirement

A regression is ACTIVE, SUPERSEDED, or RETIRED. Retirement requires sufficient current evidence that the linked proposition left scope, was replaced so the old mechanism is inapplicable, or the failure mechanism is impossible under the current evidenced architecture; current NOT_APPLICABLE status; required human authorization; independent review; an append-only retirement record; and no current baseline or product dependency. A failing, inconvenient, expensive, unavailable, or flaky regression cannot be retired for that reason. UNKNOWN legitimacy blocks. History is never deleted.

Every external operation contract declares MINIMUM_INPUT_BINDING_BASIS from APPLICATION_OBSERVED, VERIFIED_EXTERNAL, EXTERNALLY_SUPPORTED, and SELF_ASSERTED. An echoed manifest identity and per-member digests establish at most EXTERNALLY_SUPPORTED. SELF_ASSERTED or UNKNOWN cannot satisfy an operation whose contract requires byte-exact input possession, and gates derive admissibility from the recorded basis.

Every release-bearing evidence path is EVIDENCE_RECORD → OBSERVATION_RECORD → proposition or proof leaf. An observation identifies exact subject, location or measurement point, finding, method/tool, inputs and outputs, hashes, origin, submitting actor, epistemic basis, time/freshness fields, source evidence, scope, and raw-response or native-execution provenance.

Every observation has an accepted relation ESTABLISHES, REFUTES, SUPPORTS_ONLY, CONTEXT_ONLY, DOES_NOT_ADDRESS, or UNKNOWN. Only ESTABLISHES provides affirmative proof; REFUTES provides failure evidence; SUPPORTS_ONLY and CONTEXT_ONLY cannot independently satisfy a proof obligation. Normalization never elevates an external claim.

Time-sensitive evidence records observedAt, its DEVICE_REPORTED, SOURCE_ASSERTED, or VERIFIED_EXTERNAL basis, validFrom, validUntil, supersession, freshness requirement, status, and reason. Required freshness that cannot be established is UNKNOWN. Current justificatory evidence is acyclic.

VERIFIED_EXTERNAL is achieved only under a registered attestation-verification contract fixing the evidence type, the attesting tool or system identity, the verification method, the bound inputs including the operation challengeNonce or reservation, the freshness rule, and the failure semantics. Absent such a registered contract, the basis remains EXTERNALLY_SUPPORTED or weaker.

contextSourceLocations.controllingText: C1. Named structured mapping: closed-loop-raw-units-zip/1

Insert immediately after C's common raw-unit rules. This is the only structured-media mapping added by this revision. It makes the following counting choices explicit; the existence of a transport parser alone did not authorize these choices.

Every artifact preserves rawFilename and has a safe displayFilename and canonicalPath under closed-loop-filename/1. Canonical comparison uses Unicode 15.1.0 NFC, case-sensitive identity, and separately checked Unicode 15.1.0 default-case-fold and registered platform-risk collision keys. Absolute paths, drive prefixes, NUL, control characters, empty segments, `.` and `..`, duplicate canonical paths, case-fold collisions, extraction-target collisions, and supported confusable collisions are rejected. An unauthorized rename never matches solely because bytes are equal.

File extension and browser MIME type are claims. Format-dependent work records the authorized parser or adapter and detected interpretation. A materially ambiguous polyglot is BLOCKED unless one interpretation is explicitly authorized and every alternate interpretation is harmless under the operation.

Archive intake and export fail closed on traversal, absolute paths, duplicate or colliding paths, symlinks, hard links, device entries, unsupported special files, unsupported or encrypted members outside a registered encrypted contract, unsupported compression, excessive nesting, entry count, per-entry size, total compressed or expanded size, compression ratio, path depth, filename length, Unicode ambiguity, manifest mismatch, unmanifested extra members, missing members, or modified bytes. Expansion occurs only in an isolated bounded parser path and never makes content executable or prompt-visible by itself.

Every normalizer and application derivation has an immutable registry ID, version, implementation-owner file, canonical input contract, output contract, hash or build identity, and invalidation consequences. Every derived value records the exact derivation ID and source-record hashes. A changed normalizer or derivation invalidates affected current values and results unless an explicit compatibility migration proves byte- and semantic-equivalent output.

Every release-bearing derivation and normalizer is completely defined by this specification or by an explicitly named versioned normative algorithm. The semantics defined in Sections 14.6, 15, 16.1, 26, 29, 30, 31, 34.1, 34.2, and 36 control their registry entries, and an entry cannot deviate from them. A release-bearing derivation or normalizer whose semantics are not so defined is UNDEFINED_DERIVATION and blocks acceptance.
C. Insert after §6.5A: normative algorithm closed-loop-raw-units/1

The unit universe is structural accounting. Retain the exact originating input and artifact bytes; no normalized projection replaces them or asserts inspection. Each unit binds the input version, supplied occurrence, exact structural location and source-value hash. Enumerate roots in their retained source occurrence order; within a structured value visit arrays in index order and object keys in unsigned Unicode-scalar order. A canonical mirror of the same originating field is visited only once, using the originating field; separately supplied equal values are separate occurrences.

For every supplied artifact occurrence, emit one inventory unit. Where exact bytes are valid UTF-8 and the text projection re-encodes to those exact bytes, also emit physical content units: scan left to right, treating CRLF as one terminator and otherwise CR, LF or form feed as a terminator; each unit contains the span through its terminator. Retain every nonempty span, including blank lines; emit a final unterminated span if present, but no zero-length trailing span. Coordinates start at page 1/line 1; form feed increments page and resets line to 1, other terminators increment line. BOM bytes, if present, remain part of the exact projection, not silently removed. This rule is accounting, not a claim that every UTF-8 artifact's media semantics have been parsed.

For a mechanically supported structured-media subdivision, emit one structural unit per exposed page, section, archive member, embedded document/object, comment, annotation, tracked change or metadata object, using its exact parent and source locator; traverse children in source order, breaking any absent source-order tie by unsigned Unicode-scalar locator order. Recurse into textual leaves using the physical-content rule and into child media using this rule. A structural node is counted once per occurrence/location/kind; a node's structural unit and its descendant content units are distinct. Preserve inaccessible exposed nodes as INACCESSIBLE_OR_BLOCKED; do not fabricate children. Detailed coverage requires a closed format mapping that is part of this named versioned normative algorithm or an explicitly identified versioned normative format mapping authorized under §34.3. Merely publishing an implementation descriptor does not authorize such semantics. The mapping must fix node kinds, source locators, ordering, exact canonical source values and child extraction. This insertion adds no format-specific adapter or mapping. A claim of supported detailed coverage without that normative mapping is blocked; genuinely unsupported formats retain the fallback below. A mechanically available subdivision cannot be suppressed or relabeled unsupported to avoid that blocker.

Subdivision is additive: an exact UTF-8 whole-file projection emits its physical spans even when a supported structured mapping also emits structural nodes and textual leaves. Whole-file spans, structural nodes and structural textual-leaf spans have distinct kinds and locators and are all counted; overlap in underlying bytes does not deduplicate these different accounting obligations. Each archive-member or embedded-file occurrence emits both its parent structural occurrence unit and its own child inventory unit, followed by its own supported content/subdivisions. A textual leaf is not a child file and gets no inventory unit. Repeated references to the same emitted unit still deduplicate under the rule below.

Source hashes and binding are closed as follows. C(x) means the exact UTF-8 bytes of §34.1 canonical JSON; H(b) means lowercase SHA-256 hexadecimal of exact bytes b. Source-value hash preimages by kind are:

- ARTIFACT_INVENTORY: C({"byteLength":n,"contentSha256":h}), where n is exact byte length and h=H(exact artifact bytes). If bytes are unavailable, both values are null; asserted length/digest remains source context, never substituted for observed bytes. The unit remains inaccessible/blocked, with its retained occurrence/locator binding.

- PHYSICAL_SPAN: the exact original byte span including its terminator, without canonical JSON wrapping. Its locator binds zero-based byte start and exclusive end plus the one-based page/line coordinates.

- STRUCTURAL_NODE: C({"nodeKind":k,"status":q,"value":v}), where k and v are the exact kind and canonical source value fixed by the authorized format mapping, and q is ACCESSIBLE or INACCESSIBLE_OR_BLOCKED. Inaccessible nodes have v=null; exact exposed parent/locator and k remain bound. No invented serialization of an adapter object is permitted.

- STRUCTURAL_TEXT_SPAN: exact UTF-8 bytes of the mapped exact textual leaf's physical span, including its terminator. The authorized mapping identifies the leaf and its exact extraction; no silent whitespace normalization is allowed.

Each unit's binding hash preimage is C({"algorithm":"closed-loop-raw-units/1","inputVersion":V,"occurrence":O,"kind":K,"locator":L,"sourceValueSha256":S}). V is the exact owning input-version identity string; O is the ordered zero-based safe-integer path of supplied root and, where applicable, child-member occurrence indices; K is exactly one of the seven uppercase kinds above; S is the corresponding source-value hash. The unit universe is structural accounting. Retain the exact originating input and artifact bytes; no normalized projection replaces them or asserts inspection. Each unit binds the input version, supplied occurrence, exact structural location and source-value hash. Enumerate roots in their retained source occurrence order; within a structured value visit arrays in index order and object keys in unsigned Unicode-scalar order. A canonical mirror of the same originating field is visited only once, using the originating field; separately supplied equal values are separate occurrences.

For every supplied artifact occurrence, emit one inventory unit. Where exact bytes are valid UTF-8 and the text projection re-encodes to those exact bytes, also emit physical content units: scan left to right, treating CRLF as one terminator and otherwise CR, LF or form feed as a terminator; each unit contains the span through its terminator. Retain every nonempty span, including blank lines; emit a final unterminated span if present, but no zero-length trailing span. Coordinates start at page 1/line 1; form feed increments page and resets line to 1, other terminators increment line. BOM bytes, if present, remain part of the exact projection, not silently removed. This rule is accounting, not a claim that every UTF-8 artifact's media semantics have been parsed.

For a mechanically supported structured-media subdivision, emit one structural unit per exposed page, section, archive member, embedded document/object, comment, annotation, tracked change or metadata object, using its exact parent and source locator; traverse children in source order, breaking any absent source-order tie by unsigned Unicode-scalar locator order. Recurse into textual leaves using the physical-content rule and into child media using this rule. A structural node is counted once per occurrence/location/kind; a node's structural unit and its descendant content units are distinct. Preserve inaccessible exposed nodes as INACCESSIBLE_OR_BLOCKED; do not fabricate children. Detailed coverage requires a closed format mapping that is part of this named versioned normative algorithm or an explicitly identified versioned normative format mapping authorized under §34.3. Merely publishing an implementation descriptor does not authorize such semantics. The mapping must fix node kinds, source locators, ordering, exact canonical source values and child extraction. This insertion adds no format-specific adapter or mapping. A claim of supported detailed coverage without that normative mapping is blocked; genuinely unsupported formats retain the fallback below. A mechanically available subdivision cannot be suppressed or relabeled unsupported to avoid that blocker.

Subdivision is additive: an exact UTF-8 whole-file projection emits its physical spans even when a supported structured mapping also emits structural nodes and textual leaves. Whole-file spans, structural nodes and structural textual-leaf spans have distinct kinds and locators and are all counted; overlap in underlying bytes does not deduplicate these different accounting obligations. Each archive-member or embedded-file occurrence emits both its parent structural occurrence unit and its own child inventory unit, followed by its own supported content/subdivisions. A textual leaf is not a child file and gets no inventory unit. Repeated references to the same emitted unit still deduplicate under the rule below.

They require an operation reservation and file-first package. Their responseType is exactly DATA_PROPOSAL, HUMAN_INPUT_REQUIRED, BLOCKED, or EXECUTION_FAILED as permitted by the operation's field contract. - Application commands are EXECUTE_FAILURE_TEST when natively routed, EXECUTE_REGRESSION when natively routed, REGRESSION_VERIFY when natively routed, FREEZE, CONFIRM_FREEZE, COMPLETE at Stage 18, CONFIRM at Stage 19, FREEZE_BASELINE, RUN_NATIVE_TESTS, RUN_NATIVE_ATTACKS, FREEZE_DELIVERY_CANDIDATE, VERIFY_IDENTITY, CALCULATE_RELEASE, CALCULATE_EVIDENCE_CHAINS, and CALCULATE_TERMINAL. They accept no external response envelope and commit only application-owned results through the universal command path. COMPLETE at Stage 18 and CONFIRM at Stage 19 are application-calculated convergence and confirmation determinations; agents contribute only the separately declared explanatory fields of the owning record families. FREEZE, CONFIRM_FREEZE, FREEZE_BASELINE, and FREEZE_DELIVERY_CANDIDATE consume and reference the required current humanDecisions records; they never create human authority.
- HUMAN_DECISION commands are CAPTURE_DELIVERY_INTENT; application confirmation of a newly reported human-origin answer; and RECORD_HUMAN_DECISION, one global application-validated command bound to exactly one registered purpose and target per invocation. The closed RECORD_HUMAN_DECISION purpose enum is INTENT_CONFIRMATION, CANDIDATE_COMPONENT_SELECTION, BASELINE_AUTHORIZATION, DISCLOSURE_AUTHORIZATION, EXTERNAL_ACTION_RISK_AUTHORIZATION, CONTROLLED_EXCEPTION, REGRESSION_RETIREMENT_AUTHORIZATION, BACKUP_POLICY_SELECTION, TRADEOFF_OR_SCOPE_DECISION, VISUAL_BASELINE_AUTHORIZATION, and HUMAN_AUTHORITY_CORRECTION. Each purpose writes only the humanDecisions record and the human-decision-owned fields FIELD_REGISTRY declares for that purpose and target. - EXPORT_PROMPT_FILE, EXPORT_EXECUTION_PACKAGE, SELECT_RESPONSE_JSON_FILE, SELECT_RETURNED_FILES, EXPORT_OR_SHARE_AUTHORIZED_ARTIFACTS, and RECORD_DELIVERY_EVIDENCE are operator actions. They create only the application receipts and human or external evidence explicitly declared by their contracts.

For every operation, TARGET_SLOT = SHA-256(closed-loop-canonical-json/1 of contractProfileId, jobId, stage, operation, and all operation-specific target identities required by Section 14.7). The target slot excludes projectRevision so an exact retry retains its slot; expectedRevision and scopeHash remain separate mandatory preconditions. No operation can write a family or field not listed in its FIELD_REGISTRY entry.

A not-yet-due test remains registered and visible as future work but does not falsely block a prior convergence stage.

They require an operation reservation and file-first package. Their responseType is exactly DATA_PROPOSAL, HUMAN_INPUT_REQUIRED, BLOCKED, or EXECUTION_FAILED as permitted by the operation's field contract. ADVISORY_REVIEW at Stage 27 is optional and non-gating: it writes releaseGateReviews records only and cannot modify, delay, or substitute for any CALCULATE_RELEASE input, calculation, or state.
- Application commands are EXECUTE_FAILURE_TEST when natively routed, EXECUTE_REGRESSION when natively routed, REGRESSION_VERIFY when natively routed, FREEZE, CONFIRM_FREEZE, COMPLETE at Stage 18, CONFIRM at Stage 19, FREEZE_BASELINE, RUN_NATIVE_TESTS, RUN_NATIVE_ATTACKS, FREEZE_DELIVERY_CANDIDATE, VERIFY_IDENTITY, CALCULATE_RELEASE, CALCULATE_EVIDENCE_CHAINS, and CALCULATE_TERMINAL. They accept no external response envelope and commit only application-owned results through the universal command path. COMPLETE at Stage 18 and CONFIRM at Stage 19 are application-calculated convergence and confirmation determinations; agents contribute only the separately declared explanatory fields of the owning record families. FREEZE, CONFIRM_FREEZE, FREEZE_BASELINE, and FREEZE_DELIVERY_CANDIDATE consume and reference the required current humanDecisions records; they never create human authority.
- HUMAN_DECISION commands are CAPTURE_DELIVERY_INTENT; application confirmation of a newly reported human-origin answer; and RECORD_HUMAN_DECISION, one global application-validated command bound to exactly one registered purpose and target per invocation. The closed RECORD_HUMAN_DECISION purpose enum is INTENT_CONFIRMATION, CANDIDATE_COMPONENT_SELECTION, BASELINE_AUTHORIZATION, DISCLOSURE_AUTHORIZATION, EXTERNAL_ACTION_RISK_AUTHORIZATION, CONTROLLED_EXCEPTION, REGRESSION_RETIREMENT_AUTHORIZATION, BACKUP_POLICY_SELECTION, TRADEOFF_OR_SCOPE_DECISION, VISUAL_BASELINE_AUTHORIZATION, and HUMAN_AUTHORITY_CORRECTION. Each purpose writes only the humanDecisions record and the human-decision-owned fields FIELD_REGISTRY declares for that purpose and target. HUMAN commands are SAVE_HUMAN_INPUT, which creates and edits User Job Input and saves Section 18 fallback answers with their declared consequences, and RECORD_HUMAN_OBSERVATION, which records human-owned observation and evidence records for human-inspection routes. These commands write only their declared HUMAN or HUMAN_DECISION fields and records, accept no agent-owned canonical fields, and accept no external response envelope.
- EXPORT_PROMPT_FILE, EXPORT_EXECUTION_PACKAGE, SELECT_RESPONSE_JSON_FILE, SELECT_RETURNED_FILES, EXPORT_OR_SHARE_AUTHORIZED_ARTIFACTS, and RECORD_DELIVERY_EVIDENCE are operator actions. They create only the application receipts and human or external evidence explicitly declared by their contracts.

For every operation, TARGET_SLOT = SHA-256(closed-loop-canonical-json/1 of contractProfileId, jobId, stage, operation, and all operation-specific target identities required by Section 14.7). The target slot excludes projectRevision so an exact retry retains its slot; expectedRevision and scopeHash remain separate mandatory preconditions. No operation can write a family or field not listed in its FIELD_REGISTRY entry.

A failure or regression test is executed only when its target exists and its current EARLIEST_EXECUTABLE_STAGE has been reached. Its REQUIRED_BY_STAGE may not precede target availability. A not-yet-due test remains registered and visible as future work but does not falsely block a prior convergence stage.

Every negative, mutation, adversarial, storage-failure, parser-hostility, and deliberately invalid fixture executes against isolated disposable state: a test-only project clone, test-only IndexedDB namespace, immutable read-only artifact copy, isolated worker input, or explicitly authorized external sandbox. The suite must prove that no fixture mutated a canonical user project or an unauthorized third-party target. Canonical user projects and third-party systems are never mutation targets unless the exact action is separately authorized and safely bounded.

32.5 Regression retirement

A regression is ACTIVE, SUPERSEDED, or RETIRED. Retirement requires sufficient current evidence that the linked proposition left scope, was replaced so the old mechanism is inapplicable, or the failure mechanism is impossible under the current evidenced architecture; current NOT_APPLICABLE status; required human authorization; independent review; an append-only retirement record; and no current baseline or product dependency. A failing, inconvenient, expensive, unavailable, or flaky regression cannot be retired for that reason. UNKNOWN legitimacy blocks. History is never deleted.

Supported semantic compatibility and application-observed input custody remain separate facts; a supported author interpretation does not change a valid native executor into an external one.

This is the explicit current-source inclusion of exactly the 38 previously adopted conditional pairs. Historical approval identifies the preserved lineage only. Each current result must independently satisfy the current governing source and exact current identities.

Every release-bearing evidence path is EVIDENCE_RECORD → OBSERVATION_RECORD → proposition or proof leaf. An observation identifies exact subject, location or measurement point, finding, method/tool, inputs and outputs, hashes, origin, submitting actor, epistemic basis, time/freshness fields, source evidence, scope, and raw-response or native-execution provenance.

Every observation has an accepted relation ESTABLISHES, REFUTES, SUPPORTS_ONLY, CONTEXT_ONLY, DOES_NOT_ADDRESS, or UNKNOWN. Only ESTABLISHES provides affirmative proof; REFUTES provides failure evidence; SUPPORTS_ONLY and CONTEXT_ONLY cannot independently satisfy a proof obligation. Normalization never elevates an external claim.

Time-sensitive evidence records observedAt, its DEVICE_REPORTED, SOURCE_ASSERTED, or VERIFIED_EXTERNAL basis, validFrom, validUntil, supersession, freshness requirement, status, and reason. Required freshness that cannot be established is UNKNOWN. Current justificatory evidence is acyclic.

These are the existing later-than-owning-stage deferred failure-test and regression execution routes. This is not a requirement that execution has already succeeded: execution outcome, isolation, provenance, disposition and evidence sufficiency are separately determined from the actual execution. An absent or mismatched required input blocks native execution; a download, actor echo or route label does not satisfy this native minimum. This clause does not change the execution mode or permit an unapproved fallback to a different executor. Existing application, human-decision and operator commands outside these conditional pairs retain their existing source contracts; no external evidence minimum is assigned to them by this amendment.

Every external operation contract declares MINIMUM_INPUT_BINDING_BASIS from APPLICATION_OBSERVED, VERIFIED_EXTERNAL, EXTERNALLY_SUPPORTED, and SELF_ASSERTED. An echoed manifest identity and per-member digests establish at most EXTERNALLY_SUPPORTED. SELF_ASSERTED or UNKNOWN cannot satisfy an operation whose contract requires byte-exact input possession, and gates derive admissibility from the recorded basis.

Every release-bearing evidence path is EVIDENCE_RECORD → OBSERVATION_RECORD → proposition or proof leaf. An observation identifies exact subject, location or measurement point, finding, method/tool, inputs and outputs, hashes, origin, submitting actor, epistemic basis, time/freshness fields, source evidence, scope, and raw-response or native-execution provenance.

Every observation has an accepted relation ESTABLISHES, REFUTES, SUPPORTS_ONLY, CONTEXT_ONLY, DOES_NOT_ADDRESS, or UNKNOWN. Only ESTABLISHES provides affirmative proof; REFUTES provides failure evidence; SUPPORTS_ONLY and CONTEXT_ONLY cannot independently satisfy a proof obligation. Normalization never elevates an external claim.

Time-sensitive evidence records observedAt, its DEVICE_REPORTED, SOURCE_ASSERTED, or VERIFIED_EXTERNAL basis, validFrom, validUntil, supersession, freshness requirement, status, and reason. Required freshness that cannot be established is UNKNOWN. Current justificatory evidence is acyclic.

VERIFIED_EXTERNAL is achieved only under a registered attestation-verification contract fixing the evidence type, the attesting tool or system identity, the verification method, the bound inputs including the operation challengeNonce or reservation, the freshness rule, and the failure semantics. Absent such a registered contract, the basis remains EXTERNALLY_SUPPORTED or weaker.
MINIMUM_INPUT_BINDING_BASIS is EXTERNALLY_SUPPORTED for the external route of each pair in the following closed mapping:

The mapping has 88 external routes: 50 from the original §14.6 list plus 23 later failure-test and 15 later regression routes. F1's closed lists, not a wildcard allowing arbitrary operation names or stages, determine the additional pairs. The minimum does not grant operation availability or new writer authority. ADVISORY_REVIEW remains optional and non-gating.

If the applicable proof obligation, evidence contract or dimensioned-independence contract requires a stronger or distinct basis, that requirement also must be met. This generic minimum cannot weaken it, convert SUPPORTS_ONLY into ESTABLISHES, remove a required accepted review, waive unknown freshness/independence, or supply a successful result. §29.14's registered attestation-verification contract remains necessary for VERIFIED_EXTERNAL. Actual basis and its supporting observations remain recorded and evaluated by the existing gates.

These are the existing later-than-owning-stage deferred failure-test and regression execution routes. A pair is available only for a current accepted definition and its current accepted, independently reviewed execution-test binding, with established definition/test/fixture/target/outcome compatibility, the declared earliest executable stage reached, and the required current target-availability and phase conditions TRUE. Unknown, stale or unavailable prerequisites block; a legitimately future definition remains visible and unexecuted. Timing, compatibility and authority cannot be supplied by this list or inferred from a route label.

The routes remain receipt-only: one appended regressionExecutions receipt for the selected subject and ordinary supporting evidence, through the existing reserved external response path or existing isolated application-native execution path as its reviewed execution mode requires. They cannot rewrite definitions, complete unrelated ordinary stage work, expose future-stage material early, or mutate canonical user data as a test fixture. Owning Stage07/Stage15 writers and Stage17 REGRESSION permissions are unchanged. No new operation name, executor, store or canonical family is introduced.

Each execution retains exact subject/test/fixture/target identities and hashes, selected stage and operation, current scope and history activation, actual isolation and attributable raw/native provenance. Failure validation requires an actual observation establishing rejection of the bound known-invalid fixture. Regression pre-correction failure and post-correction success require distinct executions and distinct actual target input identities; one observation cannot prove both. Existing capability, risk/disclosure authorization, human review where required, compatibility, reservation, retry, replacement, receipt, freshness and restoration controls remain mandatory and cannot be bypassed by an input-basis minimum. Supported semantic compatibility and application-observed input custody remain separate facts; a supported author interpretation does not change a valid native executor into an external one.

Every external operation contract declares MINIMUM_INPUT_BINDING_BASIS from APPLICATION_OBSERVED, VERIFIED_EXTERNAL, EXTERNALLY_SUPPORTED, and SELF_ASSERTED. An echoed manifest identity and per-member digests establish at most EXTERNALLY_SUPPORTED. SELF_ASSERTED or UNKNOWN cannot satisfy an operation whose contract requires byte-exact input possession, and gates derive admissibility from the recorded basis.

Every release-bearing evidence path is EVIDENCE_RECORD → OBSERVATION_RECORD → proposition or proof leaf. An observation identifies exact subject, location or measurement point, finding, method/tool, inputs and outputs, hashes, origin, submitting actor, epistemic basis, time/freshness fields, source evidence, scope, and raw-response or native-execution provenance.

Every observation has an accepted relation ESTABLISHES, REFUTES, SUPPORTS_ONLY, CONTEXT_ONLY, DOES_NOT_ADDRESS, or UNKNOWN. Only ESTABLISHES provides affirmative proof; REFUTES provides failure evidence; SUPPORTS_ONLY and CONTEXT_ONLY cannot independently satisfy a proof obligation. Normalization never elevates an external claim.

Time-sensitive evidence records observedAt, its DEVICE_REPORTED, SOURCE_ASSERTED, or VERIFIED_EXTERNAL basis, validFrom, validUntil, supersession, freshness requirement, status, and reason. Required freshness that cannot be established is UNKNOWN. Current justificatory evidence is acyclic.

COUNT accepts only a string, array or bytes: output is respectively UTF-16 code-unit length, array element count, or byte length. It does not count Unicode scalar values or grapheme clusters. SUM, MIN and MAX accept safe-integer arrays; SUM of [] is 0 and checks each left-to-right intermediate sum for safe-integer range; MIN/MAX of [] and unsupported precision are UNDETERMINED. D1. Collections, equality and primitive outputs.

Test IR is a topologically ordered directed acyclic graph. Every step has a unique application-validated stepId, one registered op, and an explicit inputs object. Each input references exactly one literal, immutable binding, or prior step output. A step may reference only an earlier step. humanInputRequests is a required, non-null ordered array, empty allowed. Each item is a closed object with exactly these required properties: temporaryKey, question, whyRequired, affectedStageFields, affectedRecords, answerType, allowedValues; its only optional property is blocking.
